newsitem.title: USA: Mass Water Resources sets first variable rate sale.
newsitem.headline: Mass Water Resources sets first variable rate sale.

text.p: The Massachusetts Water Resources Authority on Monday said that it was planning its first sale of variable rate debt with a $170 million, negotiated offering slated for May.

Barbara Gottschalk, chief financial officer for the Authority, explained that the chance to save on interest costs led it to break with its pattern of selling fixed-rate debt. "We can afford to take on a little more rate risk and it's a way of reducing the ratepayer burden."
The Authority has approximately $3.1 billion of fixed rate debt outstanding.

However, it would not be the first one in the state to offer variable rate debt outside of a commercial paper program, as Boston's water and sewer agency already has taken this approach, the official said.

The Authority also expects a sale of $70 million to $75 million for the state revolving fund during the same period. That offering, which would be run by the Massachusetts Water Pollution Abatement Trust, likely would be negotiated as well.
In the autumn, a $300 million sale of fixed-rate revenue bonds by the Authority is planned. Another $60 million offering for the state revolving fund also is scheduled.
